was: On Mt Rushmore Road on the south side of Rapid City, the in-town option closest to the Hwy 16 run to the memorial. Roughly 128 sites: 50- and 30-amp pull-thru full hookups, 7 back-ins and 10 water-and-electric tent sites; pool, arcade, shower houses, coin laundry and wifi. Open all year, though amenities are seasonal. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: KOA on the Needles Highway (SD-87) two miles up from US-16, in the pines between Hill City and Custer State Park - the quieter alternative to the big Palmer Gulch resort. About 100 sites: deluxe patio back-ins with 50/30 amp and full hookups, other full-hookup RV sites, luxury cabins and tent sites. The small pond by the entrance sits across the highway from the campground. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Year-round park at Black Hawk on Deadwood Ave, north of Rapid City and handy to Sturgis and Deadwood. 110 full-hookup sites with 20/30/50 amp, gravel pads, pull-thru, back-in and buddy configurations, plus rustic cabins; rural setting but minutes from I-90. Black Hawk Creek runs through a tree-lined draw along the south edge, not past the sites. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Quiet, RV-only park beside Fort Hays on the Hwy 16 corridor south of Rapid City - guests must have an RV, there are no tent sites. 80 level gravel sites of 27x55 ft, pull-thru and back-in full hookups at 50/30/20 amp, hard-wired fibre internet at every site, filtered softened water, hot showers, coin laundry and fenced dog runs. Open year round. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: KOA on SD-79 north of Hot Springs, the southern-Hills base for Wind Cave, the Mammoth Site and Custer State Park's south end. About 76 sites with full-hookup RV camping, cabins and tent sites among the pines, pool and breakfast service in high summer. Open April 1 to October 31. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: On Iron Mountain Road (US-16A) between Keystone and Custer State Park, on the Mount Rushmore side of the Iron Mountain switchbacks - no TVs and limited cell service by design. Tent and RV sites plus small, medium, large, comfort and camping cabins, a small pond, new shower house and playground, and a kitchen doing pizza and sandwiches. Seasonal: mid-May through October, 2026 dates May 12 to Oct 31. The pond is ringed by cabins rather than RV sites. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Family campground a mile and a half west of Keystone in Battle Creek Canyon on Old Hill City Road, about as close to Mount Rushmore as camping gets. Around 30 sites: full hookups, water-and-electric with satellite TV, water-and-electric, electric tent sites and pop-up spots, plus standard, hilltop and sleeper cabins; pool. Season May 8 to September 27 in 2026. Canyon terrain and pine canopy - worth confirming length and levelness for a big rig. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Hilltop park on Dolan Creek Road above Sturgis, full-hookup sites with 50/30/20 amp and sewer, large sites, cabins and showers. Open May 15 to October 1 - a seasonal RV park that fills for the rally, not a rally-only camp. Good Sam Park. Satellite imagery of this address still shows pasture, so it postdates the base tiles. The most expensive tier in the Hills. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: On Avalanche Road beside I-90 at Sturgis, within sight of the rally venues but an ordinary seasonal campground the rest of the year. About 100 full-hookup big-rig sites plus back-ins, tent sites and cabins, free wifi and cable, dump station. Open mid-April to mid-October. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Resort five miles south of Sturgis off I-90 Exit 32, backing onto Black Hills National Forest and about an hour from Mount Rushmore. 156 RV sites, 20 cabins and shaded tent camping, heated pool, hot tubs, beer garden; monthly rates offered. Good Sam Park. Note it sits less than a mile from Bulldog Creek Campground (id 5818) and is a separate business - the two are easy to conflate on a map. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: 25 rustic drive-in sites plus a group camp on Indian Lake, Cloquet Valley State Forest; vault toilets, drinking water, swimming beach and boat access; no hookups, no showers. Individual sites are not reservable — same-day advance payment from 2026; the group camp reserves through MN DNR. --Claude

was: 9 rustic drive-in sites plus a group site among Gulch, Nelson and Twenty-One lakes in Paul Bunyan State Forest, managed by Lake Bemidji State Park; vault toilets, drinking water; no hookups. The lakes are non-motorized. Individual sites first-come, first-served with same-day payment; group site reserves through MN DNR. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground at the edge of Logan Valley along Big Creek, Prairie City Ranger District, near the Strawberry Mountain Wilderness. 15 sites with parking for camp trailers, first-come first-served (all Malheur NF camping is); accessible vault toilets, drinking water in summer only (off roughly October to late May), no trash service - pack it out. Fee season May-October; in winter the road is snowmobile/ski access only. No cell coverage. --Claude

was: Siuslaw NF campground along Cape Creek at Cape Perpetua, just inland of US-101 between Yachats and Florence; many sites sit on the creek. Flush toilets and drinking water, no hookups; nearest dump stations Waldport (12 mi N) or Carl G. Washburn SP (12 mi S). Mostly reservable online, a few first-come first-served. The visitor center, tide pools and 23 miles of trail are a short hike away. --Claude

was: CLOSED as of September 2026 - damaged in the 2020 Riverside Fire; the Forest Service is redesigning the Upper Clackamas campgrounds and has announced no reopening date. Check the FS page before planning. When open: large Mt. Hood NF campground on the Clackamas River 24 miles east of Estacada on Hwy 224, RV sites first-come first-served (tent sites reservable), flush toilets, dump station, amphitheater; the Clackamas River Trail starts at the upper end. --Claude

was: BLM primitive campground on the John Day River off Hwy 19/207, 10.5 miles west of Spray. Six graveled drive-in sites and two walk-to sites, first-come first-served; vault toilets, no drinking water or hookups, no reliable cell. Open year-round; pay by the QR code at the kiosk with the Recreation.gov app, or cash/check. Campfires banned June 1-October 15. Site length not published - the pads are open gravel and trailers use them, but ring the BLM Prineville District to confirm. --Claude

was: BLM primitive campground on the North Fork John Day River off Hwy 402 between Kimberly and Monument. Four sites with tables, fire rings and little shade, first-come first-served; accessible vault toilet, no drinking water or hookups; small-craft launch on the west side. Open year-round; campfires banned June 1-October 15. Site length not published - open gravel pads that trailers use, but ring the BLM Prineville District to confirm. --Claude

was: BLM primitive campground on the North Fork John Day River, 1.7 miles north of Kimberly on Hwy 402 near the John Day Fossil Beds. Five sites (one shady on the river, the rest in full sun), first-come first-served; no drinking water, hookups, garbage service or cell. Open year-round; campfires banned June 1-October 15. Not the Lone Pine Group Campground near Roseburg. Site length not published - open gravel pads, but ring the BLM Prineville District to confirm. --Claude

was: Chippewa NF campground formerly called Knutson Dam, where the Mississippi River leaves Cass Lake; 6 miles east of Cass Lake on US-2 then 5 miles north on County Road 10. 11 single sites plus 2 walk-to tent sites, vault toilets, drinking water, boat ramps on both the lake and the river, easy canoe access to the Mississippi. Reservable online in season, first-come first-served after. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground on Crow Creek beside SR-14, 11 miles east of Cedar City, at 8,100 ft under fir and aspen; 8 miles from Cedar Breaks. 18 family sites and a small group site; published lengths 25-60 ft; paved roads and spurs. Vault toilets and drinking water, no hookups or showers. A few sites are reservable online, the rest first-come, first-served. OHVs must stay trailered in the campground. --Claude

was: Small BLM campground on the Beaver River off SR-21 between Beaver and Minersville. Six first-come, first-served sites along the river, four with covered concrete-floored pavilions; fire rings, picnic tables, vault toilet; no drinking water or hookups. Site length not published: a reviewer brought a 32-ft Class C in during July 2024 but called the entry somewhat tight. --Claude

was: Small Forest Service campground on the Highway 12 Scenic Byway over Boulder Mountain, 17 miles north of Boulder and 19 south of Torrey, at 8,300 ft in ponderosa pine; about 30 miles from Capitol Reef. Nine 35-ft sites, a few reservable online and the rest first-come, first-served. Drinking water, pit toilets and dumpsters, no hookups. 16-day limit; OHVs only to come and go. --Claude

was: BLM campground on the Green River at Swaseys Rapid, 10 miles north of the town of Green River via Hastings Road, the takeout for Green River Daily floats. Nine individual sites under cottonwoods and three group sites ($50), all first-come, first-served at a self-pay station; driveways 30-60 ft. Vault toilets, fire rings and a boat ramp, no drinking water. Busy on summer weekends. --Claude

was: BLM campground and Paria Canyon trailhead at the end of 2 miles of dirt road (Monument Road 751) south of US-89 at the Paria Contact Station, 43 miles east of Kanab. Seven drive-in sites and five walk-in tent sites, first-come, first-served, open year-round; vault toilets, fire rings and picnic tables; drinking water and trash at the contact station. No site length published: reviewers report washboard and two big dips, a 21-ft trailer dragging its bumper (2019) and a 26-ft RV getting in (2020). Mostly used by Paria Canyon backpackers. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground on the Mountain Loop Highway near the South Fork Stillaguamish River east of Granite Falls, the largest on the highway. 37 RV/trailer sites (published 22-45 ft) plus a tent site in old-growth cedar, fir and hemlock; a large open field; Gold Basin Mill Pond interpretive trail across the road. Vault toilets, no water - bring your own. About half reservable, the rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground at 2,800 ft in large pine, spruce and fir near Trout Lake, on the Mt. Adams Ranger District; popular with huckleberry and mushroom pickers. 30 spacious sites on gravel spurs (published 30-40 ft) and a group site; drinking water and vault toilets. Close to the Ice Cave and Natural Bridges trails. Partly reservable online, the rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground on the east side of Mount St. Helens, named for the rock pillar beside it, a quarter mile from the Cispus River off FR 23/28. 20 semi-private sites on paved spurs (published 16-32 ft, most 24 ft or more); drinking water, vault toilets. Layser Cave and the Burley Mountain trailhead are nearby. Partly reservable, the rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground on Troublesome Creek where it meets the North Fork Skykomish River, about 20 miles east of Index on Index-Galena Road (FR 63). 18 RV/trailer sites, about ten long enough for a 23-ft rig (25-30 ft), plus 7 tent sites; potable water from a solar pump, vault toilets; all sites reservable. CLOSED: the FS lists it inaccessible because of the county's Index-Galena Road repairs and the long-term closure of FR 65 west of Jack Pass, with no reopening date (checked 2026-09-24). --Claude

was: Forest Service campground at the Middle Fork of the Salmon River launch on the edge of the Frank Church Wilderness, mostly used by rafters the night before their launch. 15 sites (5 reservable June 15-August 15, the rest first-come, first-served); RVs and trailers up to 30 ft. Reached by 25 miles (about 40 minutes) of rough, single-lane dirt road off Idaho 21 between mileposts 109-110 (Bear Valley Road); snowdrifts can close it until late May or June. Pack it in, pack it out. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground at 9,500 ft beside 14-acre Hopewell Lake on US-64 between Tres Piedras and Tierra Amarilla; the Continental Divide Trail passes through. 31 sites, of which about 13 fit a 23-ft rig (25-45 ft; the rest are 18-19 ft); two sites with horse corrals. Vault toilets, NO drinking water - bring your own. Some sites reservable, the rest first-come, first-served. OHVs must be trailered in and out. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground at the base of Laramie Peak in the Medicine Bow NF (Douglas Ranger District). 11 sites among firs, pines and aspens, most taking trailers (published 30 ft); the Laramie Peak Connector Trail starts here. Popular for OHV riding, fishing, hiking and hunting. Partly reservable online, the rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground at 10,800 ft in the Snowy Range, one of the highest in the country, off WY-130 near Libby Lake; little shade, big views of the range. 16 sites; the FS lists small trailers up to 22 ft, but reviewers have fit 25-28 ft trailers and a 38-ft Class A (site 16), so pick a larger site. Hand-pump water, vault toilet, trash; no hookups. Mix of reservable and first-come, first-served sites; 14-day limit. Acclimate if coming from low elevation. --Claude
